checked.claim: If the OPC discontinues or declines, complainant can apply to Federal Court within one year
checked.evidence: s.14(1) opens the Federal Court route after the report or a notice that the investigation was discontinued. A decision under s.12 not to investigate at all is not a discontinuance; OPC guidance links the s.14 route to the report or notice of discontinuance.
checked.replacement: If the OPC discontinues an investigation, the complainant can still apply to the Federal Court within one year of the notice of discontinuance (s.14). A decision not to investigate at all (s.12) does not open that route; judicial review of OPC conduct in the Federal Court is the general fallback.

checked.claim: Courts have explicitly said class actions are needed because the regulator is weak

checked.replacement: An Ontario court has said class actions are needed to enforce PIPEDA because the regulator cannot award damages or fine (Haikola v Personal Insurance, 2019 ONSC 5982).

checked.evidence: Federally the OPC has no fining power; money comes only from Federal Court damages and s.28 offence fines. Quebec's CAI is a provincial exception, noted in fines.imposed_by.
Federal offence fines are fixed (CAD 100,000). Quebec turnover-based caps are provincial.
